title: プロジェクトデザインⅢ（勝原基貴研究室）
subtitle: Design Project III(Katsuhara Motoki)
educationalGoal: To understand architecture with an awareness of the time axis of past, present, and future, and consider architecture, cities, and society from a historical perspective. Students will set a project theme based on their own viewpoints and problem consciousness, select an appropriate approach under the guidance of the instructor, and analyze the phenomenon, its factors, and the structure of the problem.
advice:
In Project Design III, emphasis is placed on developing the knowledge and abilities to think independently and plan, draft, and execute projects on their own through independent action by each student.
　
1) Clarification of problem interests (information gathering and discussion)
　
2) Systematic understanding of factors surrounding problems (information gathering and problem structuring)
[Previous research, literature review/field survey (related cases, case studies)]
　
3) Setting the project theme
　[Theme setting/Target area setting/Planning and drafting of the project execution plan (analysis method setting)]
　
4) Execution and coordination of projects
[Case study and analysis/visualization and structuring of analysis results, (if necessary) proposal/production/
　　Results announcement (interim review meeting (December), public presentation review meeting)]
books: No textbook is specified. Students are required to read handouts and reference books introduced during class.
requiredKnowledge:
No specific prior knowledge or skills are required, but the following attitudes toward related fields are prerequisites.
- Willingness to delve deeper into one's interests, or persistence in that effort.
- Read architecture-related books and magazines and get in touch with the latest trends in the architectural world.

activityGoals.body: To make a plan for the theme you set yourself, conduct research and collect materials, and achieve your goals.
To organize existing research, identify its problems and issues, and determine the originality of your theme.
To explore things from a variety of perspectives, including historical approaches, and consider them logically.
To present the results and key points of the creation in an easy-to-understand manner and discuss the content.
To present materials and make logical and concise statements while understanding scientific procedures.
To act independently on separately presented activities.

achievementLevels.ideal:
To be able to gather the necessary information, including relevant literature and field surveys, according to one's own interests, and to systematically explain the position of the problem and the need for its solution in the field concerned.
To be able to consider and set up appropriate research and analysis methods according to the objectives of the project, and to promote the project systematically and effectively.
To be able to logically summarize the results obtained and communicate them to others in an easy-to-understand manner.
achievementLevels.standard:
To be able to gather necessary information on one's own problems and concerns through relevant literature research, field visits, etc., and to explain them.
To be able to set up an appropriate methodology for the purpose of the project (problem solving) and carry out the project.
To summarize and explain the results obtained.
